title: The factor borrowed from relativity
spoken: The Lorentz factor equals one divided by the square root of one minus the squared speed ratio.
explanation: The Lorentz factor is defined here in modern notation. Using it for the light energy imports the relativity result; it does not independently derive that result.
assumptions: Two equal, opposite light pulses remove total positive energy L; their symmetry removes recoil in the body’s rest frame.
The two inertial descriptions refer to the same emission and the same body boundary; |v| < c.
These are authored modern teaching equations, not a transcription or printed-notation concordance.

notes.title: Same observer speed
notes.explanation: v is the signed relative speed between inertial descriptions. Its magnitude is less than c. It is held fixed while the body emits.

notes.title: Modern SI speed of light
notes.explanation: c denotes the speed of light in modern SI notation. A normalized model with c = 1 is a different unit convention and cannot supply values labeled metres per second.

notes.title: Compare the speed with c
notes.explanation: v/c is dimensionless. Its sign gives the relative direction; squaring removes that direction.

notes.title: Square the speed ratio
notes.explanation: Both positive and negative observer speeds give the same square. The low-speed expansion uses this small dimensionless number.

notes.title: One minus the squared speed ratio
notes.explanation: This quantity stays positive for an admitted observer and approaches zero at the excluded light-speed boundary.

notes.title: Take the positive square root
notes.explanation: For |v| < c the radicand is positive. The boundary |v| = c is not an allowed inertial observer.

notes.title: Modern Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: γ depends on the observer speed. In this modern teaching notation γ is the factor, not the speed ratio v/c. The transformation of the light energy is imported from relativity, not derived from these energy accounts.

notes.title: Take the reciprocal
notes.explanation: The positive reciprocal is at least one. This definition alone says nothing about a body’s rest energy.

notes.title: What this relation asserts
notes.explanation: The Lorentz factor is defined here in modern notation. Using it for the light energy imports the relativity result; it does not independently derive that result.

sentence.text: The Lorentz factor equals one divided by the square root of one minus the squared speed ratio.
